{{Quote|Nord, listen. Don't worry about the other ships. Why don't you watch the security patrols and tell me when they swap shifts, and I'll worry about Haathi-stuff.''"<br />"''Define 'Haathi-stuff'.''"<br />"''Everything else.''"<br />"''That's what worries me.|Haathi and Dren Nord converse on Zelos II|<ref name="Ship Jackers" />}}
'''T'Charek Haathi''' was a [[Wroonian/Legends|Wroonian]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] who served the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] as both a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] and [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|Special Operations]] team leader. Born on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Wroona/Legends|Wroona]], Haathi deplored stability and being bored. She served with the [[Wroonian defense force]], but the rigidity of military life led Haathi and her [[Unidentified Wroonian defense force starfighter squadron|unit]] to go rogue and target [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] shipping. The [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] was decimated in a reprisal attack from the Empire, and Haathi eventually joined the Alliance shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] alongside two [[Human/Legends|Humans]] she had met on the planet [[Rodaj]]: former Imperial [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Ivhin Jayme]], and [[Technician/Legends|technical]] genius [[Morgan Q. Raventhorn]]. A stint in the Alliance's [[Alliance Starfighter Corps/Legends|Starfighter Corps]] led to the same problems that Haathi had encountered serving with the Wroonians, although she was regarded as one of the Alliance's top pilots.

As she faced discipline and authority problems, Haathi's superiors decided to transfer her to [[Special Operations]], where she could use her considerable skill-set in a more unregulated [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. Haathi recruited her friends Jayme and Raventhorn into her new [[T'Charek Haathi's Special Ops team|team]], and they came to specialize in stealing [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. The team was highly successful, and Haathi found her place in the Alliance. Accompanied by a Human [[Medic/Legends|medic]], [[Dren Nord]], the team stole a [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]], [[The Maker (YT-1300 light freighter)|''The Maker'']], from a [[Unidentified spaceport (Zelos II)|spaceport]] on the planet [[Zelos II]]. Taking the ship to an Alliance [[Drop Point: Gelgelar|drop point]] on the planet [[Gelgelar/Legends|Gelgelar]], the team was forced to face the [[Doom Slayer]], an experimental [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] that the ship's previous owner, the [[Sluissi]] [[Sythluss Leethe]], had created and kept aboard the vessel. Although defeated, the Doom Slayer had a [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destruct mechanism]] built in; the team barely escaped from the drop point in ''The Maker'' before the installation was destroyed, though they managed to evacuate most of the base personnel.

==Biography==
===Early life===
T'Charek Haathi, a [[Wroonian/Legends|Wroonian]] [[Gender/Legends|female]], was born on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Wroona/Legends|Wroona]]<ref name="Ship Jackers" /> in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]].<ref name="TEAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> In her youth, Haathi worked with her [[T'Charek Haathi's grandmother|grandmother]], who ran a successful shipping company on Wroona. Haathi hated being both stable and predictable, and craved excitement and adventure; the work left her constantly bored. She applied to the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] in an effort to find some excitement, despite the fact that she knew she would be subject to constant prejudice due to being both female and non-[[Human/Legends|Human]]. Her application was denied, but she was recruited by the [[Wroonian defense force]] when she was eighteen. A [[Standard year/Legends|year]] later, Haathi was a qualified [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] operating within a [[Unidentified Wroonian defense force starfighter squadron|squadron]]. However, regimented life in the military was not to Haathi's tastes either, as her duties mainly consisted of patrolling Wroona. Eventually, her [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] went rogue and began raiding [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] corporate [[Starship/Legends|ships]]. Their assaults were bold, but they drew the attention of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], who struck back against Haathi's unit. The squadron was decimated, but Haathi survived the assault and managed to make it to the planet [[Rodaj]] in the Inner Rim. There, she found work as a [[Mining/Legends|miner]] and struck up a friendship with two Humans: former Imperial [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Ivhin Jayme]], and former [[Scout/Legends|scout]] and [[Technician/Legends|technician]] [[Morgan Q. Raventhorn]]. Feeling down in her current situation, Haathi and Jayme decided that they would join the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]], and convinced Raventhorn to go with them.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

===Rebel Alliance service===
{{Quote|Would you like me to say this for the eighty billionth time? Rebellion needs ships. We steal ship. Take home to base.|T'Charek Haathi, to Dren Nord|<ref name="Ship Jackers" />}}
[[File:Arik_Stijhl.jpg|thumb|right|Colonel Arik Stijhl, who butted heads with Haathi during her time as a Flight Instructor]]
Haathi and her companions enlisted with the Rebel Alliance shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], and she was assigned to the [[Alliance Starfighter Corps/Legends|Alliance Starfighter Corps]] flying a [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighter]]. Although her experience and abilities made Haathi one of the Alliance's best pilots, her carefree attitude towards regulations and her impulsiveness grated on her superior [[Officer/Legends|officers]]. The Alliance was in retreat following the Battle of Yavin, hiding from Imperial forces and regrouping their strength. Haathi found the situation monotonous and livened up her duties by sabotaging her Y-wing's systems at random just to see how well she could fly without them, yelling "Eject!" into open [[Comm unit/Legends|comm]] channels simply to find who would trigger their [[Ejector seat/Legends|ejection seat]], and constantly referring to her [[T'Charek Haathi's commanding officer|commanding officer]] as "[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Nerf/Legends|Nerf]]" just to see how long it would take for him to get mad. Haathi endured several suspensions from flight duty, which just made her more bored and annoying to others than she already was, and finally her [[Commander/Legends|commanding]] officer began to ignore her completely rather than punish her.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

At some point, Haathi was made a [[Flight instructor/Legends|flight instructor]] and posted to a [[Unidentified Alliance training base|training base]]. There, she came into conflict with the local Human [[Quartermaster/Legends|quartermaster]], [[Arik Stijhl]]. Stijhl, a veteran logistics officer, was a stickler for regulations and [[Time/Legends|timetables]], and Haathi was the complete opposite. Her training sessions often called for the unauthorized requisition of supplies, which, in Stijhl's mind, undermined his authority as the base's supply officer.<ref name="Drop Points">{{JournalCite|14|Special Ops: Drop Points}}</ref> Eventually, her superiors decided to transfer her to [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|Special Operations]]. They saw it as a double positive situation&mdash;the Rebellion would be able to retain Haathi's considerable skills, but the Starfighter Corps would be rid of her. Haathi agreed to the reassignment.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

Placed in command of a [[T'Charek Haathi's Special Ops team|Special Ops team]], Haathi immediately recruited her former colleagues Ivhin Jayme and Morgan Raventhorn into her squad, along with a [[Medic/Legends|medic]]. Haathi's team was based out of an [[Unidentified Alliance base (Derricon)|Alliance base]] on the planet [[Derricon]],<ref name="Ship Jackers" /> in the [[Spirva sector/Legends|Spirva sector]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]],<ref name="TEAOC" /> and engaged in shipjacking operations. Although answerable to the [[Unidentified Rebel base commander|base commander]] on the world, Haathi and her team were allowed free rein once off-base. Her actions in the field earned her a promotion from [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] to [[Major/Legends|Major]]. Over the course of six [[Standard month/Legends|months]], Haathi either fired or lost eight medics in turn until she was assigned [[Dren Nord]], a Human former [[Doctor/Legends|surgeon]] with the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]], despite her protests. Haathi was assured that Nord had experience of field work, but she had her doubts.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

=====Zelos II=====
{{Quote|Fine. Okay, I just want you to know, I think this is a bad idea.''"<br />"''Really?''"<br />"''Don't you?''"<br />"''No. I ''know'' this is a bad idea.''"<br />"''Then why don't we call it off before anybody breaks into anything and, ah&hellip;anybody gets, you know, shot?''"<br />"''It's too late for that. He called to me.''"<br />"''Who called to you? 'Master Fate?<nowiki>'</nowiki>''"<br />"''Him. The ship. It said, 'T'Charek! T'Charek! Save me from these ugly black market nerf-heads! I need a real pilot inside me. I need a rewiring job.' What am I supposed to say? 'No? Sorry, ship, but my new med-tech thinks we should get that slag heap to your left because nobody's guarding it and there aren't any security alarms wired to it?' Is that what I should say to that ship out there? Look at him!|Dren Nord and T'Charek Haathi, discussing Haathi's method of target selection|<ref name="Ship Jackers" />}}
[[File:Haathi1-AJ13.jpg|thumb|left|250px|T'Charek Haathi surveys her target.]]
In search of starships to procure for the Alliance, Haathi took the team to [[Zelos II]],<ref name="Ship Jackers" /> a planet in the [[Tyus sector/Legends|Tyus sector]] of the Mid Rim.<ref name="TEAOC" /> Targeting a [[Unidentified spaceport (Zelos II)|spaceport]], the team acquired stolen technician uniforms and obtained a set of the installation's remodeling plans that provided information on its security systems. Haathi's plan called for infiltrating the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] at night to take advantage of the native [[Zelosian]]s' pathological fear of the dark. She reasoned that the spaceport guards would be more concerned with the darkness around them and thinking of the moment that their shift would end, rather than be focused on actually guarding the spaceport. Using the stolen uniforms and forged work orders to fool [[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoid]] and [[Droid/Legends|droid]] personnel alike, the team infiltrated the base, and Haathi evaluated the potential targets. Out of hundreds of ships in the spaceport, there were dozens of [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighters]]&mdash;top of the Alliance's list of ships to procure&mdash;berthed in the spaceport. At least two were relatively unguarded, while a third was located beneath a guard tower, in full view of several [[Security camera/Legends|security cameras]], and surrounded by a [[forcefield cube]], a mesh-link [[Power fence/Legends|power fence]], and a [[blast wall]]. Haathi, seeing both the inherent challenge and pure excitement in stealing the most heavily guarded ship in the spaceport, selected it as their target.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

Haathi led Jayme and Nord to a maintenance tower overlooking the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] while Raventhorn ascended a lighting tower; her task was to [[Slicer/Legends|splice]] into the spaceport's systems to rewire the security camera covering the vessel to display a [[Computer/Legends|computer]]-generated video of the [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighter's]] [[Hangar/Legends|docking bay]] with the ship undisturbed to mask the team's approach. Haathi and Nord monitored the spaceport's security patrols from the maintenance tower to make sure that they did not discover Raventhorn and blow her cover. Meanwhile, Jayme rewired the backup security computers located in the maintenance tower so that the unit would be under the team's complete control. From their hiding spot, Nord questioned Haathi's decision to take the most heavily guarded ship in the spaceport; her response&mdash;that taking any other vessel would have been boring&mdash;left him unconvinced.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

Raventhorn completed her task, and began playing the fake video over the security monitors. With the cameras disabled, Haathi ordered Jayme to head down to the docking bay while Raventhorn attached a [[Scomp-Spiker]] to the security systems. When Jayme signaled that he was in position, Raventhorn triggered the device, sending a power surge through the main security computer that temporarily disabled the forcefield cube and power fence encircling the ship. The spaceport's systems rerouted to the backup computer that Jayme had rigged earlier; the modifications made to the unit kept the security systems offline for a short time before the auxiliary power kicked in and re-established both the forcefield and power fence. Jayme pole-vaulted the fence and wall, landing just as the power to the security fields was reactivated. Inside the docking bay, Jayme relayed the ship's identification numbers to Haathi, who identified the vessel as [[The Maker (YT-1300 light freighter)|''The Maker'']], owned by a [[Sluissi]] called [[Sythluss Leethe]].<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

[[File:Haathi2-AJ13.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Haathi is shocked by the stun steps on ''The Maker''.]]
Using a [[VoiceBox Speech Pattern Duplicator|VoiceBox]], Jayme deactivated the security systems from inside to admit Haathi and the rest of the team. Momentarily lost in admiring the ship, Haathi soon ordered Raventhorn to begin work on disabling the freighter's security systems while Jayme and Nord kept an [[Eye/Legends|eye]] on the security patrols. Soon enough, Raventhorn announced that the security systems would be disabled once she had disconnected the [[Ramp Entry Security System|stun steps]]. Haathi, in her enthusiasm to take the ship, had only heard that the defenses were down and began bounding up the entry ramp. The freighter's stun steps triggered as her foot touched the ramp, generating an electromagnetic neuro-shock field that knocked her unconscious and sent her flying backwards. Haathi came to rest in the open, and Jayme ordered Raventhorn to get Haathi under cover quickly. Nord, meanwhile, abandoned cover to see if Haathi required his assistance and was was spotted by one of the security guards on the catwalks above. A ladder from the catwalks was lowered into the bay, and the security guards descended, [[Lightfight|firing]] on the Special Ops team.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

Haathi regained consciousness to find herself under ''The Maker'', protected from the incoming fire by the entry ramp. She had no feeling in her [[Limb/Legends|legs]], and Raventhorn told her to stay put before disappearing. As feeling began to return to her legs, Haathi maneuvered herself to survey the situation. The guards were trading [[Laser/Legends|laser]] fire with her team, who were in cover behind [[Cargo container/Legends|cargo crates]]. No member of her team had been injured yet, despite the fact that the guards' [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] were set to [[Death/Legends|kill]] while her team were firing [[Stun/Legends|stun]] blasts. Haathi started to wonder if the effort to take ''The Maker'' had been worth it; catching herself and refusing to think along those lines, she resolved not to let the guards rob her of her prize and issued orders to fall back to the ship. Suddenly, Nord, having set his own weapon to kill, hit one of the security guards. Haathi immediately ordered him to switch back to the stun setting, which he refused to do unless she could get them out of trouble. Haathi ordered Jayme to stun him; when the [[Commando/Legends|commando]] began to comply, Nord ducked into cover and followed orders.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

The guards in the docking bay began to thin out, as several had retreated to the upper level, where they were better positioned than Haathi's team. Haathi ordered Raventhorn to finish disabling the stun steps so they could board the ship and escape. As Raventhorn worked, a [[Unidentified Zelosian security guard|security guard]] opened fire on her. The technician was blocking Haathi's line of sight to the guard, preventing her from using her own weapon to neutralize him. Haathi feared the worst until Raventhorn hit the guard with two cables attached to the stun steps, stunning him with an electromagnetic neuro-shock field. Seeing this, Haathi ordered Raventhorn to use the cables to charge the metal ladder rungs, which in turn sent the stun blast surging through the metal catwalk attached to it. The neuro-shock field stunned the remaining guards.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

As the team began to fall back to ''The Maker'', Jayme helped Haathi to her feet and into the ship. Heading for the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]], the team were confronted with a sealed hatch. Haathi groaned, Raventhorn began to figure out a way past it, and Jayme simply attached [[Compund Flex-5 Detonite Tape|detonite tape]] to the door, then used a shot from his blaster to detonate it. The resulting explosion disengaged the hatch's locking mechanism, admitting Haathi into the cockpit. Dropping into the pilot's seat, Haathi rerouted all power to the [[Engine/Legends|engines]] and launched the freighter as security reinforcements took pot shots at the departing ship.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

=====Gelgelar=====
{{Quote|I just gave clearance at Ready-One to a light freighter.''"<br />"''And?''"<br />"''It's registered as ''The Maker''. The call-sign belongs to a Major T'Charek&mdash;''"<br />"''Haathi.''"<br />"''That's right. [Pause] Sir?''"<br />"''Yes, Kovings.''"<br />"''I should have said 'no' to her request, right?''"<br />"''No, it's okay. You shouldn't have said 'no.' You should have opened fire.|[[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Bendlar Kovings]] and Colonel Stijhl discuss Haathi's arrival on Gelgelar|<ref name="Drop Points" />}}
[[File:Themakerfreighter.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Haathi's latest acquisition, ''The Maker'']]
Haathi flew ''The Maker'' to an Alliance [[Drop Point: Gelgelar|drop point]] on the planet [[Gelgelar/Legends|Gelgelar]],<ref name="Drop Points" /> in the [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEAOC" /> The drop point was commanded by Arik Stijhl, and Haathi's main reason for stopping at the base was solely to show off her new ship and promotion to Major to him. Stijhl begrudgingly welcomed Haathi, Jayme, and Nord to Gelgelar, where Haathi was disappointed to learn that Stijhl was no longer a Major himself, and had since been promoted to [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]]. Haathi claimed to need supplies to cover her true reason for visiting; Stijhl summoned his Human administrative [[Aide/Legends|aide]], [[Maglenna Pendower]], to take their requisition needs. Raventhorn, who had been working on the freighter's faulty power grid, commed Haathi to inform her of something. Just as she was about to, static erupted from the comm, and the entire ship lost power. As the emergency lighting kicked in, Pendower headed straight for the maintenance bay where Raventhorn was working. Haathi ordered Jayme to follow Pendower, then headed off the ship in search of Nord, who had exited the ship just after meeting Stijhl.<ref name="Drop Points" />

After finding Nord, Haathi returned to ''The Maker'' to find that Pendower had revived Raventhorn, who had been seemingly electrified by a surge from the power grid. Pendower believed it was clearly an accident, but Jayme disagreed. While Pendower helped Nord to take Raventhorn to the drop point's medical bay, Jayme followed his hunch that Raventhorn's mishap had not been accidental. Haathi, meanwhile, attempted to repair ''The Maker''{{'s}} power grid. Unable to understand Raventhorn's notes on the original malfunction, Haathi was relieved when Stijhl offered assistance in the form of [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Nofre Ecls]], a [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]]. While Stijhl left to investigate a commotion outside, Haathi and Ecls began to work on the power grid. Ecls was of the opinion that she would need to rewire the entire grid to get the ship functional again, a job that would take several [[Standard day/Legends|days]]. Haathi suggested just hot-wiring the ship, but Ecls advised against it since a single power surge would destroy the entire freighter. The Major was forced to order the Sullustan engineer to rewire the power grid.<ref name="Drop Points" />

[[File:Haathi3-AJ14.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Haathi and Ihvim Jayme help Maglenna Pendower aboard ''The Maker''.]]
Outside, an experimental [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]], the [[Doom Slayer]], had been activated. Hidden aboard ''The Maker'' by its creator, Sythluss Leethe, it began its primary mission of wiping out all organic lifeforms in the immediate area. Jayme had been correct in his assumption that Raventhorn's mishap was not an accident and had begun tracking the droid and combating it alongside the drop point's security personnel. The droid had locked the base's hangar doors and scrambled the comm channels. Stijhl ordered an evacuation of the base, directing the base personnel to board ''The Maker'' to make their escape. Haathi and Ecls succeeded in restoring power to the ship, and the freighter began to fill up with wounded personnel. Haathi found a pilot and told him to go to the cockpit and take off the minute the engines came back on-line. Haathi went to the boarding ramp, exposing herself to acrid smoke while she waited for any sign of her team. Nord appeared shortly thereafter, supporting an injured Stijhl. Haathi helped him bring the Colonel aboard, inquiring if Nord had seen the others, which he had not. The ship's [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]] began to fire just as Haathi saw Jayme, Raventhorn, and Pendower, each supporting the other as they tried to run for the ship. Haathi helped the three aboard just as ''The Maker'' lifted off. Jayme had succeeded in defeating the Doom Slayer, but the [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] droid had been equipped with a [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destruct mechanism]]. ''The Maker'' smashed through the closed hangar doors, speeding away from the drop point as the bomb exploded and destroyed the base.<ref name="Drop Points" />

On board a medical [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]], Haathi and her team learned the origins of the assassin droid, and Stijhl reprimanded them for the loss of the supplies located at the drop point, which included 6 industrial-grade [[Power generator/Legends|power generators]], 600 medical field packs, 82 [[Perimeter sensor/Legends|perimeter sensor]]s, 8 [[B1-series worker droid]]s, and 200 [[Blaster power pack/Legends|blaster packs]]. He then informed them that they were going on an acquisition run to recover the losses. Haathi agreed on the condition that Pendower&mdash;who had impressed Haathi by helping to treat Raventhorn and assisting Jayme&mdash;was assigned to her team in place of Nord, who had not lived up to her standards. Stijhl agreed to the transfer and allowed the team to leave.<ref name="Drop Points" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|T'Charek! How many fingers am I holding up?''"<br />"''Muh&mdash;Morgan?''"<br />"''How many fingers?''"<br />"''Autumn.''"<br />"''Close enough.|Morgan Raventhorn tests Haathi's reactions after the latter is stunned|<ref name="Ship Jackers" />}}
T'Charek Haathi was an easygoing, quick-witted woman who enjoyed having fun and taking chances. Easily bored, she loathed stability and predictability and was always on the lookout for opportunities that would challenge and excite her.<ref name="Ship Jackers" /> In personality, she was a typical energetic, carefree, Wroonian who relished finding new challenges.<ref name="Alien Encounters">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> Considered to be short for her [[Species/Legends|species]], Haathi stood as tall as an average Human female. Enthusiastic and impulsive, she had a flippant manner which often annoyed other beings. Haathi had a problem with authority figures, but was herself a natural leader. Despite this, she was not power hungry and hated pulling [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] on others unless the situation necessitated it, mainly because she feared becoming the authority figure that she had always opposed. A capable tactician and planner, Haathi was not opposed to listening to the suggestions of her team when it came to mission planning. She trusted two of her team&mdash;Ivhin Jayme and Morgan Raventhorn&mdash;implicitly and made a conscious effort to give Dren Nord the benefit of the doubt when he first joined her unit,<ref name="Ship Jackers" /> but when he failed to measure up to her standards, she quickly sought a replacement for him.<ref name="Drop Points" /> Despite her trust in her friends' skills, she worried about them and placed their well-being above the needs of the Rebel Alliance,<ref name="Ship Jackers" /> such as when Raventhorn needed better medical attention than a drop point could provide.<ref name="Drop Points" /> Haathi was reluctant to use lethal force when it was not necessary, as she refused to authorize her team to kill the guards at the Zelos II spaceport despite the fact that they were using kill shots instead of stun blasts against them. She became angry when one of her team, Nord, disregarded her order and used his blaster's kill setting. She went as far as ordering Jayme to stun him to prevent Nord from doing further harm.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

A skilled pilot, Haathi specialized in flying Y-wing starfighters and was fully capable of repairing them when the need arose. She was trained to fly space [[Transport/Legends|transports]], and could use the weapon, [[Deflector shield/Legends|shield]], and [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] systems on them effectively. She was able to repair ships and their weapons, and could repair [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]]. Haathi was able to [[Astrogation/Legends|navigate]] through [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], and she was particularly knowledgeable about locations in the Inner Rim. She knew about business and had an interest in [[Alien/Legends|alien]] languages and [[Star system/Legends|planetary systems]]. Haathi's work as a Special Operations operative naturally lent itself to undercover work, and she was able to use her skills to either intimidate or persuade individuals into revealing information, or to con them out of something. She could use her talents to research and investigate potential targets, figuring out the best way to obtain what she needed.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

Working as a ship jacker, Haathi was particularly adept at determining the value of starships, and she had a working knowledge of [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement]] procedures and security systems. Haathi carried two weapons, a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]], and a [[Heavy blaster pistol/Legends|heavy blaster pistol]], and knew how to wield them effectively. She could repair her weapons, and was skilled in the use of vehicle-mounted blasters. She was trained in unarmed combat. Usually, Haathi carried a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] in addition to her weapons, as well as several fake [[ident chit]]s.<ref name="Ship Jackers" />

==Behind the scenes==
T'Charek Haathi first appeared in ''[[Special Ops: Ship Jackers]]'', in issue [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 13|13]] of [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'', the first in a series of articles detailing the Alliance Special Operations.<ref name="Ship Jackers" /> Haathi's adventure's were due to continue in ''[[Special Ops: The Art of Infiltration]]'', to be published in [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 17|issue 17]], but the ''Adventure Journal'' was cancelled before the issue was released. All three installments were written by [[John Beyer]] and [[Kathy Burdette]].<ref name="Infiltration">{{JournalCite|17|Special Ops: The Art of Infiltration}}</ref>

===Cut content===
{{Cutstart}}
For a [[Standard week/Legends|week]] after the incident on Gelgelar, Haathi and her team remained under medical supervision on the frigate, where Haathi spent most of the time worrying about the injuries that Jayme and Pendower had suffered, or checking to make sure that Raventhorn had not gone back into cardiac arrest. Haathi herself required six [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] on a ventilator to combat the effects of breathing in too much toxic smoke.<ref name="Infiltration" />

Two weeks later, Haathi and her team headed to the planet [[Laertos]]. An Imperial [[Zonith Field|supply depot]] was under construction on the world, and Haathi had devised a plan to infiltrate the base and steal a [[super freighter]] loaded with supplies. Intelligence from [[General/Legends|General]] [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]] indicated that the base's security consisted of a two-[[Meter/Legends|meter]] mesh fence, two guards, and around a hundred construction workers. On arrival, it was discovered that the base was undergoing a major upgrade into a full [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]], and was protected by a fully-charged mesh-link fence, [[Mine/Legends|minefield]], and heavy [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser turrets]] with a clear field of vision. Undeterred, Haathi, Raventhorn, and Pendower posed as picnicking locals in the woods surrounding the base, distracting a [[Patrol 1138|five-man patrol]] and allowing Jayme to incapacitate all five using a [[Tranq 25 HV Pistol]] modified for use as a [[Blaster carbine/Legends|carbine]]. Relieving the [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] of their uniforms and equipments, the team stole the patrol's [[LD5 Land Speeder|patrol speeder]] and infiltrated the facility, which forced Haathi to use [[Color/Legends|green]] [[camouflage field paint]] to disguise her blue skin.<ref name="Infiltration" />

With Pendower posing as a major, the team headed to the administration building. During the infiltration, Haathi switched the plan. Instead of hijacking a super freighter, Haathi had Pendower change the routing orders for future shipments of high-value material and equipment to be delivered to small, out of the way Imperial bases close to Alliance outposts that could then be raided with minimal effort. To cover their tracks, Haathi had Jayme and Raventhorn blow up the obvious parts of the base that an inexperienced [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] would target. However, both teams were caught in the act by Imperial security forces under the command of Captain [[Edmond Mylesgood]], who had been alerted to a possible unauthorized presence on the base when the patrol that Haathi's team had impersonated failed to follow proper procedure and check in. A lightfight ensued, but the team was able to extradite themselves from danger and exfiltrate from the base.<ref name="Infiltration" />
